title: Clinical outcome analysis: an end-to-end pipeline
text: classifyResponder() applies Beaton dual rule: change true responder exceeds MDC (real change beyond measurement error) MCID (clinically important change). use Fugl-Meyer upper extremity (FMA-UE) score, whose store entry carries MDC (6.65 points, derived Wagner 2008 SEM) MCID (4.25 points, Page 2012). MDC exceeds MCID, change can clinically important yet still inside measurement error:
code: cols <- c("change", "mdc", "mcid", "classification") # a 6-point gain: past the MCID, but not past the MDC -> measurement error classifyResponder(baseline = 30, followup = 36, instrument = "FMA-UE",                   population = "chronic_stroke_minimal",                   direction = "increase")[, cols] #>   MDC = 6.65, MCID = 4.25 #>  #>     true_responder subclinical_change  measurement_error      non_responder  #>                  0                  0                  1                  0 # a 9-point gain: past both thresholds -> a true responder classifyResponder(baseline = 30, followup = 39, instrument = "FMA-UE",                   population = "chronic_stroke_minimal",                   direction = "increase")[, cols] #>   MDC = 6.65, MCID = 4.25 #>  #>     true_responder subclinical_change  measurement_error      non_responder  #>                  1                  0                  0                  0

title: PhysioClinical 0.1.0
text: End--end clinical outcome pipeline (see Clinical outcome analysis vignette): score instrument, benchmark published clinimetrics, classify response (dual MDC-vs-MCID), compute normative z-score, score goal attainment, tag ICF, export FHIR. Data-driven scoring validated instruments (Berg, FMA-UE/LE, ARAT, NIHSS, mRS, MAS, WMFT, FIM, FAM) timed performance tests (10mWT, 6MWT, TUG). clinimetric store published MDC/MCID/SEM/ICC constants (DOI), classifyResponder() dual responder classification, governed normative references normativeZScore(). Goal Attainment Scaling (defineGoal() / scoreGAS()). Responder classification minimal detectable change (MDC): mdcResponder() labels change scores (follow-minus baseline) "improved", "stable", "declined", treating change real improvement decline exceeds measurement noise. MDC threshold derived standard error measurement (sem_value) configurable confidence level (default 0.95) via PhysioCore::mdc(), classification stays consistent shared psychometric kernels ecosystem.
